headline: US Department of Defense driving structural demand for additive manufacturing in submarine supply chain, creating capacity shortfall
reasoning: The US Navy determined it needed to increase submarine production from 1.2 to 2.4 submarines per year and concluded additive manufacturing was the only way to achieve that speed. Traditional manufacturing of certain parts takes two years, whereas additive manufacturing can produce the same parts in 16 weeks. There is not enough additive manufacturing capacity in the existing supply chain, which is creating strong demand for systems and parts providers. This structural shortfall is expected to drive rapid growth in the short to medium term.
quote: Yeah, it actually is critical parts. And what we're finding those it's been driven by the US Department of Defense, US Navy. So what they determined was they needed to increase the submarine production up from 1.2 subs to 2.4 a year, and they determined that the only way that they could do that was by going additive manufacturing because of the speed of manufacturing. So a great example is we produce the part 4 or 5 parts for the US Navy for the submarine program in about 16 weeks, and it would typically take them two years to get that same part manufactured by traditional means.
episode_title: AML3D ramps up defence push with US Navy growth

headline: AML3D CEO Sean Ebert flags accelerating US Navy contract growth and confidence in company execution despite share price underperformance
reasoning: Sean Ebert notes AML3D has multiple systems deployed with the US Navy and at Oak Ridge, and expects that footprint to grow rapidly. Management and the board are pleased with how the company is growing, which Ebert says will be reflected in the upcoming full-year financial results. Despite acknowledging frustration at the share price failing to gain traction, Ebert says the focus remains on executing the strategy, which is rolling out well in the short, medium and long term.
quote: Well, look, it is frustrating, but I guess, look, our view is that we're just focused on executing the work that's in front of us. Uh, we've got a really clear strategy in the short, medium and long term to grow the company. Uh, that's rolling out and playing out quite well. So management and board are actually really pleased with the way that the company is growing. And that's reflected in the financial performance of the company, which you'll see at the end of the financial year when we post our results.
episode_title: AML3D ramps up defence push with US Navy growth

headline: AUKUS framework creating manufacturing opportunities across Australia, US, and UK for defence-aligned suppliers
reasoning: AUKUS is creating a trilateral manufacturing and supply opportunity for companies able to operate across all three jurisdictions. AML3D has operations in Ohio serving the US defence market and Australian operations serving both the US and UK. A $1.2 million contract with BAE Systems UK was signed for quality qualification work on alloys and parts manufacturing. This triumvirate positioning is seen as a significant strategic advantage as AUKUS industrial demand expands.
quote: Well, Aukus is actually pretty instrumental to us because we're also manufacturing out of Australia. So we're manufacturing out of the US from our US operation located in Ohio. And that's dedicated to serve the US defense market. And then we're also manufacturing out of Australia not only for the US but also for the UK market. So one of the things we did under Aukus was we signed a deal with the $1.2 million contract with BA UK, and that was to do a quality qualification of works on a series of alloys, as well as manufacturing of certain parts for them. And that's starting to expand. So we've got the triumvirate sort of position by being in Australia as well as us and being able to deliver into the UK under Aukus.
episode_title: AML3D ramps up defence push with US Navy growth

headline: AML3D CEO flags record orders and 70% revenue growth expected in FY27, underpinned by US Navy submarine program
reasoning: AML3D finished FY26 with 16.8 million in orders rolling into FY27, representing the highest order level in the company's history at 29 million peak. Cash receipts of 10.4 million were up 20% year on year, with revenues expected to grow upwards of 70% year on year. The company has a 26.8 million cash balance, with 12 million allocated to doubling the US facility and 5 million for a UK technology centre. The US Navy is driving demand for additive manufacturing to increase submarine production from 1.2 to 2.4 per year, and AML3D is a direct supplier of critical parts into that supply chain. The company is also diversifying into oil, gas, and aerospace sectors in the US.
quote: Well, it's been a pretty exciting time for us. We finished quarter four with 16.8 million in orders rolling into FY 27. So we're really confident about having a really strong year in FY 27. Uh, in FY 26, we actually peaked. We had a peak in orders at 29 million. So that's the highest level of orders that we've ever had in the company. We're expecting revenues to be upwards of sort of 70% a year on year when we release our financials in the next sort of month or so. In terms of cash balance, we have 26.8 million cash at bank. We've allocated 12 million of that to build out the US and effectively double the size of the US facility.
episode_title: AML3D ramps up defence push with US Navy growth
